agree.reason: The plain apology that names the missing refund and the single short email speaks directly to this household's grievance, but nothing says what happens to their $540 if hail hits again, so a resistant reader may still hold back.

honest.reason: Every fact comes from the brief, and the 'three weeks of produce' is a fair derivation, though 'came half full' drops the brief's 'about'.

works_the_facts.reason: Turning six half-full weeks into about three lost weeks is good work, but the email never puts a dollar figure on the loss (about $74 at roughly $24.50 a week), and it never puts the $31,000 in terms of what members get from it.

right_comparison.reason: Last season is described accurately, but the email never sets a storm year under the new setup (second field, nets) against last July, so the reader can't see how much difference the changes would make.

qualification.reason: 'I can't stop storms' is an honest hedge, and the email gives a concrete date (March 15) and a share count (52), but it never says what members would get if a crop failure happened anyway.

objections.reason: The silence and the apology are dealt with, but the reader's main objection, getting no refund or credit when the farm falls short, isn't answered: pause credit covers the member's absences, not the farm's crop losses, and nothing commits the farm to communicating better next time.

fit.reason: It's a short, well-organized email of about 180 words, under the 200-word limit, with a clear subject line and a clear call to action.
